methodology: This is a dated, curated evidence desk, not a census of all funding or all NGOs. Each displayed record links to the original source.
Publication date, academic/fiscal reference period and retrieval date are different fields. Unknown publication dates remain unknown.
A government-school stock change is openings minus removals plus reporting, management and boundary changes; it cannot identify individual closure events.
Population comparisons need matching geography, boundaries, age group, period and sources. Total population growth and projected population alone cannot establish rising local demand for schools.

Government approval, release, expenditure, NGO receipts, programme outlays and equity commitments are distinct stages. Monetary rows must not be summed across stages, currencies, periods or nested funding envelopes.

National sources appear as context under state filters. A city/district text search matches explicit source content and mapped places; no city allocation is inferred from an organisation headquarters.
coverageNotes: The numeric school-stock panel covers all 36 states/UTs and all 75 Uttar Pradesh districts, plus a national aggregate, for 2021-22 to 2025-26.
The 38 source records are a bounded research collection retrieved 6 October 2026; coverage is neither exhaustive nor live.
Private and aided schools, colleges, NGOs, CSR, foreign grants and private capital have source and programme coverage; comparable institution-level funding ledgers are not yet assembled.
City mentions show documented programme or platform presence. No city monetary allocation or matched city child-population series has been verified.
All recorded investigation leads are questions to reconcile, not findings of corruption, unlawful closure or denied access.

leads.title: Ghaziabad district: reconcile fewer reported schools with catchment demand
leads.summary: Match school IDs and administrative orders, then compare 6–14 population and accessible public seats within the same catchments. Not established: Closures despite rising child population or denial of access.
leads.signal: Government-school stock declined from 504 in 2021-22 to 474 in 2025-26; 493 to 474 in the last year.
leads.falsifier: Close the access-loss hypothesis if school-code continuity and receiving-school records show recoding only, unchanged reachable capacity, and no increase in travel burden for the same child catchments.

leads.title: Jhansi district: identify the schools behind the count change
leads.summary: Review 39 net fewer reported schools in 2025-26, distinguishing merges, recoding, closures and newly opened schools. Not established: 39 individual schools closed.
leads.signal: Government-school stock fell from 1,504 in 2021-22 to 1,450 in 2025-26; 1,489 to 1,450 in the last year.
leads.falsifier: Reject the individual-closure interpretation if a campus-level crosswalk shows the 39 net change is accounted for by composite-school recoding or classification changes with teaching sites still operating.

leads.title: Meghalaya: audit a sharp one-year reporting change
leads.summary: Reconcile all management categories and school-code transitions before treating the change as an access loss. Not established: 2,169 school closures or a funding irregularity.
leads.signal: Government-school stock moves from 7,789 in 2024-25 to 5,620 in 2025-26, a net difference of −2,169.
leads.falsifier: Resolve the reporting anomaly if cross-category school-code transitions fully account for the decrease and confirm that teaching locations and accessible seats did not disappear.

leads.title: Telangana: resolve the change in reported government schools
leads.summary: Check comparability and destination capacity before investigating whether particular growth areas have lost accessible seats. Not established: Population growth has outstripped school provision.
leads.signal: Government-school stock falls from 30,057 in 2024-25 to 28,088 in 2025-26, a net difference of −1,969.
leads.falsifier: Reject an access-loss interpretation if linked institution histories account for the count decrease and comparable catchments retain sufficient reachable capacity without longer journeys.

leads.title: Uttar Pradesh: trace approved-to-released funding differences
leads.summary: Reconcile sanction ledgers and release conditions across the same fiscal period before attributing delays or calculating school-level spending. Not established: Missing money, misuse or district-level underfunding.
leads.signal: FY 2025-26 Samagra approved central share ₹5,892.4327 crore versus released ₹5,622.1515 crore; PM SHRI approved ₹377.63 crore versus released ₹236.22 crore.
leads.falsifier: Close the funding-gap concern if sanction conditions, carry-forward balances and dated release ledgers reconcile the differences with no overdue eligible release.

leads.title: Chhattisgarh: preserve revised PAB versions and avoid double counting
leads.summary: Link original and revised approvals, label superseded values, and separate spillover, planned releases and actual disbursements. Not established: Budget inflation or unauthorised spending.
leads.signal: 7 July 2025 revision incorporates supplementary approvals; total plan ₹232,029.17 lakh includes ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover.
leads.falsifier: Reject double-counting if the revision audit shows original items were superseded, spillover was carried once, and the final sanction ledger matches the revised approved plan.

leads.title: Higher education: compare funding access with government and aided eligibility
leads.summary: Join approved institutions to AISHE IDs and eligible categories, then compare underserved district coverage without implying private unaided colleges are entitled to this scheme. Not established: All college types receive comparable government grants.
leads.signal: PM-USHA covers government and government-aided state HEIs; AISHE 2023-24 reports 17.1% government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided among responding colleges.
leads.falsifier: Reject unequal coverage among eligible institutions if matched AISHE IDs and allocation records show apparent gaps arise from ineligible categories, duplicate approval units or non-response.

leads.title: Use child population before flagging closures in growing places
leads.summary: Flag only when school/catchment event data and age-specific demand are comparable; display evidence strength and missing inputs. Not established: A general logical contradiction between total population growth and lower school counts.
leads.signal: Official demographic projections allow rising total population alongside falling national ages 5–14 population.
leads.falsifier: Reject the apparent demographic contradiction when same-boundary school-age population falls or stays stable despite total-population growth; otherwise obtain school-level access evidence.

leads.title: Uttar Pradesh school pairing: preserve codes and track where classes operate
leads.summary: Reported concern: Children and parents challenged school pairing and access conditions. Government response: Minister says nearby pairing improves teaching, retains posts and UDISE codes, exempts difficult routes and may be reversed if demand grows. Next check: Retrieve latest appellate order and school-wise pairing/restoration list; measure actual class location and travel burden.
leads.signal: Policy and implementation dispute; historical interim court reporting
alternativeExplanations: Minister says nearby pairing improves teaching, retains posts and UDISE codes, exempts difficult routes and may be reversed if demand grows.
Legal school identity, physical teaching location and administrative merger can describe different events.
leads.falsifier: Comparable school-level evidence shows no increased access burden or all questioned pairings were restored.

leads.title: Honganuru KPS pilot: transport and access require school-level verification
leads.summary: Reported concern: Student organisations and educationists question rural access from moving classes into a magnet school. Government response: Circular cited in reporting promises transport; minister later says no government schools will be shut. Next check: Obtain BEO circular, transfer dates, transport uptime and capacity; distinguish legal school identity from physical location of classes.
leads.signal: Reported seven-school pilot and competing policy descriptions
alternativeExplanations: Circular cited in reporting promises transport; minister later says no government schools will be shut.
Legal school identity, physical teaching location and administrative merger can describe different events.
leads.falsifier: Proposed transfers did not occur or verified equivalent access is maintained.

leads.title: Himachal rationalisation: separate zero-enrolment denotification from merger
leads.summary: Reported concern: Consolidation could increase travel burden where nearby school accessibility is weak. Government response: Reported rationale is zero/very low enrolment; difficult-terrain and tribal schools were exempted. Next check: Retrieve notifications and receiving-school travel/attendance records; retain 100 denotified and 120 merged as separate reported actions.
leads.signal: Reported completed administrative actions, original orders pending
alternativeExplanations: Reported rationale is zero/very low enrolment; difficult-terrain and tribal schools were exempted.
Legal school identity, physical teaching location and administrative merger can describe different events.
leads.falsifier: Notification or exemptions contradict reported counts or affected schools retain service at the same location.

leads.title: Follow the money once across donor and recipient accounts
leads.summary: Join donors, implementing organisations and institution receipts before comparing geographic education funding.
leads.signal: CSR, philanthropy and foreign grants can appear in both donor expenditure and recipient income statements.
alternativeExplanations: Two disclosures may describe the same transfer.
Programme costs may span education and other sectors.
Registered offices and project sites may differ.
leads.falsifier: Unique transaction references, matched donor–recipient periods and project locations reconcile the amounts without duplicate counting.
